name: Leaning Cable Lateral Raise
description: A cable lateral raise performed while the lifter leans away from the pulley, anchoring one hand on the cable column for support. The lean creates a longer moment arm at the beginning of the movement (where free-weight lateral raises are easiest) and provides constant tension throughout, making it superior to dumbbell lateral raises for medial deltoid development.

execution.starting_position: Stand sideways to the cable pulley, gripping the upright with the near hand for support. The far hand holds the cable handle.
execution.setup_instructions: Attach a single handle to the low cable pulley. Stand sideways, lean away from the machine, and grip the cable handle with the far hand.
steps: Step 1: Lean away from the cable to create a natural stretch on the medial deltoid.
Step 2: Raise the arm upward and out to the side until it is horizontal or slightly above.
Step 3: Hold briefly at the top, squeezing the medial deltoid.
Step 4: Lower under control back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to swing the arm up instead of controlled deltoid abduction
Allowing the torso to rotate during the raise
safety_considerations: The cable provides constant tension even at the bottom — this is the advantage over dumbbells
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arm raised to horizontal or slightly above at the top. Full arm by the side at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Raise with the deltoid, not the trap
